To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cell size in S. pombe is regulated through the size-dependent expression and dilution of the mitotic activator C25, creating a mechanism by which cells trigger mitotic entry when they reach a size-dependent threshold concentration of C25.
cell size in fission yeast is regulated by a size-dependent mechanism that controls the expression of the mitotic activator cdc25.
cell size homeostasis in fission yeast is maintained by a size-dependent expression of Cdc25, the mitotic activator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that control cell size.
the mechanism of cell size control in fission yeast.
the mechanisms that regulate the timing of cell division.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cell size is regulated in fission yeast through a size-dependent mechanism that regulates mitotic activator levels, and this is likely to be a general mechanism for cell size regulation in eukaryotic organisms.
the mechanism for size control in fission yeast is the size-dependent expression of Cdc25.
the mechanism of size control in fission yeast is the size-dependent regulation of the mitotic activator Cdk1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the mitotic activator Cdk1-Cdc25 in fission yeast is regulated by a size-dependent mechanism that is distinct from that of budding yeast and bacteria, and that this mechanism may be conserved in eukaryotic size control.
the mitotic activator, Cdc25, is regulated in a size-dependent manner and this regulation is important for cell size homeostasis.
cell size in fission yeast is regulated by a novel strategy: the size-dependent transcriptional expression of the mitotic activator cdc25.
The main takeaway from our work is that
size control in fission yeast is not a simple adder or inhibitor dilution model, but rather a size dependent expression of the mitotic activator, Cdc25.
the mechanism of size control in S. pombe is different from the mechanism in budding yeast.
size-dependent expression of Cdc25 provides an elegant mechanism to regulate cell size in fission yeast, and that this mechanism may be conserved in other eukaryotes, including humans.
